stack: React 18 + Vite, Firebase (Google sign-in, Firestore), Playwright e2e tests in demo mode, node:test process tests, GitHub Pages

idea.intent: A library of 90 ready-to-use AI prompts for BAs, POs and PMs, with an admin to write, review and publish them

decisions.title: Static site on GitHub Pages with Firebase as the only backend
decisions.context: BAPO Path is a free learning site run by one person. Decided before Compass; recorded in the 2026-11-26 back-fill.
decisions.decision: Host the React/Vite build on GitHub Pages and use Firebase (Google sign-in + Firestore). No server code.
decisions.consequences: Anything needing a server needs another free option. Access control must live in firestore.rules.

decisions.title: New user-facing features ship behind default-off feature flags
decisions.context: Changes reach learners as soon as they merge; the Owner wants to try them first. Recorded from CLAUDE.md.
decisions.decision: Every new user-facing feature gets a flag in src/data/flags.js, off by default with audience owner, then moves owner → beta → everyone.
decisions.consequences: Every feature PR adds a flag; the Owner moves audiences in Prompt admin → Insights → Features.

decisions.title: Security lives in firestore.rules, with a test for every rule change
decisions.context: Hiding something in the UI is not access control. Recorded from CLAUDE.md.
decisions.decision: Every permission is enforced in firestore.rules and tested in tests/rules.test.mjs; a rule is never weakened to make a feature work.
decisions.consequences: Rules changes need the Owner to approve (compass/REVIEW.md) and the production deploy approval.

decisions.title: Hash routing, so no in-page #anchors
decisions.context: Bug #27: landing page links like href="#roadmap" were read as routes and bounced to the top.
decisions.decision: Keep hash routing (#/path) for GitHub Pages; scroll to sections with JavaScript instead of #section anchors.
decisions.consequences: Reviewers flag any href="#…" that is not a route.

decisions.title: Adopt the Compass Framework, as used in travel-map
decisions.context: The Owner asked to make the AI-native SDLC of this repo similar to travel-map, which uses Compass: intent, requirements, design, plan, enforced guardrails, independent review and an always-current handover.
decisions.decision: Add compass/ (spec.json as source of truth, generated views, checks, guardrails, edit hook, plans, intents, designs, REVIEW.md) and AGENTS.md, adapted to BAPO Path: Playwright TC titles, the prompts check, firestore.rules tests and the existing CI jobs.
decisions.consequences: Requirements move from docs/requirements/ to compass/spec.json. From REQ-026 on, every requirement needs an approved intent and design, and every code PR a plan file and an independent review.

decisions.title: Agents merge their own PRs once CI is green and the independent review approves
decisions.context: travel-map lets the agent merge once CI is green and the independent review says APPROVE. The Owner chose the same for BAPO Path in chat on 2026-11-26 ("please let the agent merge"), replacing the earlier rule that the Owner merges every PR.
decisions.decision: After CI is green and a fresh reviewer posts APPROVE for the head commit, the author agent squash-merges with node compass/merge-pr.mjs <n> and then reports to the Owner. PRs listed under "What a person still decides" in compass/REVIEW.md (protected paths, firestore.rules, deletions, dependencies, learner data, sign-in or roles) need the Owner's explicit OK in chat first; the agent quotes it in a PR comment, adds the human-approved label and then merges (confirmed by the Owner on 2026-11-26). CHANGES NEEDED is never merged.
decisions.consequences: The Owner is told about changes after the merge and rolls flags out as before. Agents open PRs as ready for review (a draft cannot be merged). merge-pr refuses protected paths, rules changes and deletions without the label, and bug fixes without a reviewer's test-first run. The label cannot prove the Owner said yes: agents add it only after an explicit OK in chat. A session without an authenticated gh CLI checks the same conditions by hand and merges with the GitHub tool pinned to the reviewed head commit.

decisions.title: Compass checks run as a separate CI workflow; existing job names stay
decisions.context: Branch protection may already require the checks "Content, build and end-to-end tests" and "rules"; renaming them would block every PR.
decisions.decision: Add .github/workflows/compass.yml with a job named "Compass checks" (spec, guardrails, plan, test-first, process tests) and leave ci.yml and rules-test.yml as they are.
decisions.consequences: The Owner adds "Compass checks" to the required checks in branch protection. merge-pr requires all three.

decisions.title: "PM" in the learning roadmap means Product Manager
decisions.context: "PM" can mean Project Manager or Product Manager. The site already has PMBOK terms and Project Kickoff prompts.
decisions.decision: The Owner chose Product Manager for the new track (REQ-036), at the same depth as the BA and PO tracks, behind the pmTrack flag (audience owner).
decisions.consequences: The PM track teaches discovery, strategy, metrics and launch. Project-management topics stay in the PMBOK glossary. A Project Manager track would be a separate requirement.

requirements.title: One source of truth for requirements, tests and handover
requirements.story: As the Owner I want requirements, test cases and decisions in one file with generated views, so that any person or agent can see where the project stands.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given compass/spec.json
When I run node compass/check-spec.mjs
Then it fails if a requirement (not Draft) has no test case, a test case points to an unknown requirement, or an automated test case's file does not carry its TC id

Given I changed compass/spec.json
When I run node compass/build-views.mjs
Then requirements.md, tests.md, decisions.md and handover.md are regenerated, and check-spec fails in CI while handover.md is stale

requirements.title: Enforce the guardrails automatically
requirements.story: As the Owner I want the agent rules enforced by machines, so that protected files, secrets and oversized changes cannot slip through.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given an agent in Claude Code
When it edits a protected or forbidden path in compass/guardrails.json, or writes text that looks like a secret
Then the edit hook stops the edit and asks for the Owner's approval in chat (a reminder: the CI check with the human-approved label is the real gate)

Given a pull request
When it changes more than 12 files, a forbidden path, or (without the human-approved label) a protected path, a deletion or a dependency
Then the CI guardrails check fails, using main's copy of the check and its rules

requirements.title: Independent review of every pull request
requirements.story: As the Owner I want every PR reviewed by an agent that did not write it, so that the author never approves its own work.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given a pull request
When it is ready to merge
Then a fresh reviewer has posted '## Independent review (Claude)' with a verdict and the reviewed commit, as described in compass/REVIEW.md

Given node compass/merge-pr.mjs <n>
When CI is not green, the latest trusted review is not APPROVE for the head commit, a bug fix's review has no Test-first run that failed, or a protected path, firestore.rules or a deletion has no human-approved label
Then it refuses to merge and says why

requirements.title: Capture the business need as an intent before requirements
requirements.story: As the Owner I want my request written down as a measurable intent that I approve, so that the reason behind every requirement stays next to the code.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given a requirement from REQ-026 on
When check-spec runs
Then it fails unless the requirement points to an Approved compass/intent/ file that lists it and keeps the Owner's words under '## Business need'

requirements.title: Approved design before any code
requirements.story: As the Owner I want to approve how a change will look before it is built, so that misunderstandings are caught before coding.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given a requirement from REQ-026 on that is not Draft
When check-spec runs
Then it fails unless the requirement has a design file in compass/design/ that mentions it, or 'none: <reason>'

Given a requirement In build or Done
When its design file is not 'Status: Approved'
Then check-spec fails (no code before the design is approved)

requirements.title: A written plan before code
requirements.story: As the Owner I want each code change to start from a short plan, so that the reviewer can check the diff against what was intended.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given a change that touches code
When node compass/plan-file.mjs or merge-pr runs
Then it fails unless the change adds compass/plans/<REQ-ids>-<name>.md with real Files, Steps, Risks and Proof

Given a pull request that touches code
When the CI guardrails check runs
Then it fails unless the PR body has a '## Plan' with Files, Steps, Risks and Proof filled in

requirements.title: Failing test committed before every bug fix
requirements.story: As the Owner I want each bug fix to start with a test that fails, so that we know the fix really fixes the bug.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given a pull request with the bug label
When compass/test-first.mjs runs in CI
Then it fails unless the first commit only adds a test under tests/ (plus its plan file in compass/plans/), later commits do not edit that test, and a node test from the first commit fails at that commit

requirements.title: Record decisions as ADRs
requirements.story: As the Owner I want decisions I make in chat recorded with their reasons, so that later sessions do not undo them.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given spec.json decisions
When check-spec runs
Then every ADR has id, date, title, status (Proposed, Accepted, Superseded or Rejected), context, decision and consequences, and links only to known requirements

requirements.title: Shared memory for agents: lessons learned and working knowledge
requirements.story: As the Owner I want agents to learn from repeated mistakes, so that I do not correct the same thing twice.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-26
ac:
Given CLAUDE.md
When the process tests run
Then it has a 'Lessons learned' section, imports compass/agent-knowledge.md, and stays under one page

Given the repo skills in .claude/skills/
When the process tests run
Then each has a 'Use when' description and names the check that enforces it

requirements.title: Product Manager role and learning path
requirements.story: As a starter Product Manager I want to choose "Product Manager" when I join and follow a PM skill roadmap from Beginner to Expert, so that I learn the skills for my role and not only BA or PO ones.
requirements.source: Requested by the Owner in chat on 2026-11-27
ac:
Given the pmTrack flag is on for me
When I open onboarding step 1
Then I see three role cards (Business Analyst, Product Owner, Product Manager), and picking Product Manager and a level then Continue saves PM as my track

Given my track is Product Manager
When I open the Skill Roadmap
Then the Product Manager tab is selected and shows four levels (Beginner → Expert) with full Beginner lessons, short skills above and a challenge at the end of each level, my starting level unlocked

Given I am on the PM track
When I gain XP
Then my rank uses PM names: Intern → Associate PM → Product Manager → Senior PM → Lead PM

Given the pmTrack flag is off for me
When I open onboarding, the Roadmap, search or a term page
Then I see only BA and PO, as today
